title: Topological Superconducting Phases in a Strained Altermagnet-Superconductor Heterostructure
authors: Keita Yoshizawa, Ryo Okugawa, Takami Tohyama
abstract: We investigate topological superconductivity in a heterostructure consisting of a two-dimensional $s$-wave superconductor and a $d$-wave altermagnet with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. In particular, we study the effects of strain and hopping anisotropy on the topological superconducting phases. By calculating the Chern number, we obtain topological phase diagrams as functions of the chemical potential and the strength of the effective magnetic field induced by the magnetic proximity effect. We find that strain-induced lattice distortion allows topological superconducting phases to emerge over a broad parameter region. Our findings suggest that strain that lowers symmetry can serve as a route to realizing topological superconductivity in altermagnet-superconductor heterostructures.
summary: This theoretical study explores topological superconductivity in an altermagnet-superconductor heterostructure, focusing on the role of strain and hopping anisotropy. By calculating the Chern number, the authors demonstrate that structural distortions can induce robust topological phases. This work suggests that strain offers a powerful, controllable route to realizing topological superconductivity in magnetic heterostructures.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence and control of topological superconductivity within a heterostructure composed of an s-wave superconductor and a d-wave altermagnet.
main_result: Strain-induced lattice distortion and hopping anisotropy are shown to be effective mechanisms that allow topological superconducting phases with high Chern numbers (up to |C|=2) to emerge over broad parameter regions.
method: The authors calculate the Chern number using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian and confirm the topological nature by observing gapless Majorana edge modes under open boundary conditions.
model_or_system: The system is a 2D heterostructure combining an s-wave superconductor and a d-wave altermagnet, modeled using the Bogoliubov–de Gennes Hamiltonian. The model incorporates strain effects via a parameter 'b' and Rashba spin-orbit coupling.
key_observables: Topological phase diagrams characterized by the Chern number (C), and the existence of gapless Majorana edge modes.
important_parameters: Strain parameter (b), chemical potential ($\mu$), and hopping anisotropy ($t_x$ vs $t_y$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes fixed parameters for the superconducting gap ($\Delta_s$) and spin-orbit coupling ($\alpha$), and simplifies gap closing analysis by setting $\sin k_x = \sin k_y = 0$ at high-symmetry points.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the heterostructure, the momentum dependence of the effective magnetic field under strain, the resulting topological phase diagrams showing |C| regions, and energy spectra confirming gapless Majorana edge modes.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the model Hamiltonian, calculating the Chern number to map out topological phase diagrams as a function of strain and anisotropy, and finally confirming the physical realization of the topological phases via the detection of Majorana edge modes.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between lattice strain (a structural parameter) and the realization of exotic topological superconducting states is highly relevant for designing novel quantum materials and superconducting devices.
